title: Silicone Oil in Vitreoretinal Surgery: A Comprehensive Clinical Compendium
summary: Silicone oil is a long-term endotamponade agent utilized for complex retinal detachments. Mastering its indications, ocular complications, and precise removal techniques is essential for the modern vitreoretinal surgeon.

sections.title: Definition & Indications
content: Definition: High-viscosity, clear, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) used as an internal tamponade.
Indications: Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy (PVR), Giant Retinal Tears (GRT), CMV Retinitis-related detachments, and trauma.
Physical Properties: Hydrophobic, non-absorbable, chemically inert, and refractive index of 1.40.

sections.title: Ocular Complications
content: Secondary Glaucoma: Pupillary block or emulsification-induced trabecular meshwork obstruction.
Band Keratopathy: Prolonged corneal contact in phakic or aphakic eyes.
Cataract Formation: Inevitable in phakic eyes due to metabolic isolation of the lens.
Emulsification: Formation of micro-droplets leading to oil migration into the anterior chamber.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: 1. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy (check for oil droplets/pupillary block).
2. Intraocular pressure (Goldmann/Tonopen, watch for rapid spikes).
3. Gonioscopy (evaluate for emulsified oil in the angle).
4. B-Scan Ultrasonography (detect retro-oil or posterior staphyloma).
5. OCT (assess macular status through oil).

sections.title: Removal Protocol
content: Step 1: Perform complete vitrectomy and membrane peeling.
Step 2: Utilize a passive aspiration cannula or active pump at low suction (e.g., 200-300 mmHg).
Step 3: Consider use of viscous fluid injector (VFI) if oil is highly viscous (5000 cSt).
Step 4: Perform final fluid-air exchange to clear residual micro-droplets.

content.explanation: P: Pressure check (glaucoma?), R: Retinal integrity (attachment confirmed?), E: Emulsification check (angle evaluation), P: Patience (avoid rapid aspiration to prevent iatrogenic tears).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always perform a peripheral iridectomy (PI) in inferior position for aphakic eyes to prevent pupillary block.
Avoid using silicone oil if the patient requires frequent MRI imaging (though some are safe, check protocols).
Oil emulsification is correlated with the duration of time left in the eye and eye movement frequency.
Silicone oil is not a substitute for complete relief of vitreous traction.
